{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Clara Latimer Bacon''' (13 August 1866 – 14 April 1948) was a mathematician and professor of mathematics at [[Goucher College]]. She was the first woman to earn a PhD in mathematics from [[Johns Hopkins University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|at=[https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA54 p. 54]|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|title-link=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics|last1=Green|first1=Judy|last2=LaDuke|first2=Jeanne|date=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=9780821843765|language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Bacon was the daughter of Larkin Crouch Bacon and Louisa Latimer. She was born in Hills Grove, [[McDonough County, Illinois]],<ref>[https://mathwomen.agnesscott.org/women/bacon.htm Clara Latimer Bacon] in ''Biographies of Women Mathematicians''</ref> the eldest of her parents four children. She also had four other half siblings. <ref>{{cite web | url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Bacon_Clara/ | title=Clara Bacon - Biography }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf|title=SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL FOR PIONEERING WOMEN IN AMERICAN MATHEMATICS: THE PRE-1940 PHD'S|last1=Green|first1=Judy|last2=LaDuke|first2=Jeanne|date=2016|website=American Mathematical Society|access-date=12 October 2018}}</ref>
Bacon attended North Abingdon High School and begun her college life at Hedding Collegiate Seminary.

She graduated from [[Hedding College]] in [[Abingdon, Illinois]], in 1886 with a bachelor's degree (the degree of PhB). She achieved a second bachelor's degree from [[Wellesley College]] in 1890. Later, Bacon taught in a private school in Litchfield, Kentucky and in three different schools over seven years. Bacon studied for her master's degree at the [[University of Chicago]], completing her thesis in 1903 and graduating in September 1904, after six summers of study while continuing to work full time at the Woman's College of Baltimore.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> 

In 1907, Johns Hopkins University had been admitted the women officially. Bacon applied to Hopkins at the same time. She achieved her PhD from Johns Hopkins University in 1911, one of only four women to receive a PhD from the university that year, the first year that women were granted PhDs without special approval from the trustees.<ref name=":1" /> At Johns Hopkins, Bacon was a student of the [[Geometry|geometer]] [[Frank Morley]], who was her dissertation adviser.<ref name=":0" /> Her thesis was published in ''[[American Journal of Mathematics]]'' in 1913.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|title=Women in mathematics : celebrating the centennial of the Mathematical Association of America|isbn=9783319666945|location=Cham, Switzerland|pages=313|oclc=1015215187|last1 = Beery|first1 = Janet L.|author1-link= Janet Beery |last2=Greenwald|first2=Sarah J.|last3=Jensen-Vallin|first3=Jacqueline A.|author3-link=Jacqueline Jensen-Vallin|last4=Mast|first4=Maura B.|author4-link=Maura Mast|date=2017-12-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bacon|first=Clara Latimer|date=1913|title=The Cartesian Oval and the Elliptic Functions p and σ|journal=American Journal of Mathematics|volume=35|issue=3|pages=261–280|doi=10.2307/2370311|jstor=2370311}}</ref> Her research in her master's and PhD theses was on [[Euclidean geometry|planar geometry]].<ref name=":2" />

She was emeritus professor of mathematics at Goucher College, formerly known as Women's College Baltimore, in [[Maryland]], US,<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|title=DR, CLARA L. BACON|date=16 April 1948|work=Special to The New York Times|id={{ProQuest|108419753}}}}</ref> after working on the faculty from 1897 to 1934.<ref name=":0" /> She began teaching there in 1897, at the invitation of Dr [[John Franklin Goucher]], and in 1905 became an associate professor, and in 1914 a full professor.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/bacon.htm|title=Clara Latimer Bacon|website=www.agnesscott.edu|access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref>
Bacon was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name=":4" /> She was president of the Baltimore chapter of the [[American Association of University Professors]]<ref name=":1" /> and supported the [[League of Women Voters]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.biography-center.com/biographies/4060-bacon_clara_latimer.html|title=Biographies of Clara Latimer Bacon Mathematicians|website=www.biography-center.com|access-date=2018-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181018002955/http://www.biography-center.com/biographies/4060-bacon_clara_latimer.html|archive-date=2018-10-18|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

A student hall of residence at Goucher College, Bacon House, is named in her honour.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goucher.edu/experience/where-you-live/residence-halls/mary-fisher-hall|title=Mary Fisher Hall {{!}} Goucher College|website=Goucher College|language=en|access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref>

She died on 14 April 1948, aged 81.<ref name=":3" />
